subject: maths
question:
PBA and PDC are two secants. AD is the diameter of the circle with the centre at O. ∠A = 30°, ∠P = 20°. Find the measure of ∠DBC.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/454496cc8df3528f65dea1bbb4d6b3eedb5d3f81f73dfccae801d490f58f71f3.png]
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In **triangle PAD**, we have ∠P = 20° and ∠A = 30°.

Exterior ∠ODC at **vertex D** = ∠P + ∠A = 20° + 30° = 50°.

In **isosceles triangle OCD** (where OC = OD = radius), ∠OCD = ∠ODC = 50°.

Center angle ∠COD = 180° − (50° + 50°) = 80°.

Measure of ∠DBC = ∠DAC (Angles in same segment) = ∠COD ÷ 2 = 80° ÷ 2 = 40°.

**∴ The correct answer is 40°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** ∠A = 30°, ∠P = 20°, and **AD** is the **diameter** of the circle with center **O**.

**Formula Used:** Sum of angles in a **triangle** is 180°; Angles subtended by the same **arc** at the circumference are equal; Angle at the **center** is twice the angle at the **circumference**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/01aef6aa22c065b1ff3328b4dead48d2fd7d12beaf041f3f9bd0273d6d9dca25.png] 

In **ΔPAD**:

⇒ ∠PDA = 180° − (∠APD + ∠PAD)

⇒ ∠PDA = 180° − (20° + 30°) = 130°

⇒ ∠ODC = 180° − ∠PDA = 180° − 130° = 50° (Linear pair on secant **PDC**)

In **ΔOCD** (where **OC = OD** as radii):

⇒ ∠OCD = ∠ODC = 50° (Angles opposite to equal sides)

⇒ ∠COD = 180° − (50° + 50°) = 80°

∠DAC is the angle at the circumference subtended by **arc CD**:

⇒ ∠DAC = (1 ÷ 2) × ∠COD = 80° ÷ 2 = 40°

∠DBC and ∠DAC are angles in the **same segment** subtended by **arc CD**:

⇒ ∠DBC = ∠DAC = 40°

**∴ The correct answer is 40°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle in a Semicircle

The angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circumference of the circle is always a right angle (90°).

Angles in the Same Segment

Angles subtended by the same chord or arc at the circumference in the same segment of a circle are equal.

Central Angle Theorem

The angle subtended by an arc at the center of a circle is double the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circle.</p
